cls: Antineoplastic - HER2-targeted bispecific monoclonal antibody (biparatopic ECD2 and ECD4)
pharm: Bispecific antibody binding two distinct HER2 extracellular domains (ECD2 and ECD4); blocks HER2 signaling, induces receptor internalization, and mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity; used in HER2-positive biliary tract and gastric/GEJ cancers

summary: Zanidatamab (Ziihera) is a HER2-targeted bispecific monoclonal antibody that binds two distinct HER2 extracellular domains (ECD2 and ECD4) on the same receptor. By dual-epitope binding it inhibits HER2-driven signaling, promotes receptor clustering and internalization, and recruits immune effector killing of HER2-positive tumor cells. It is indicated for adults with previously treated unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer, and for HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. The dose is 20 mg/kg by intravenous infusion every 2 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, with premedication to reduce infusion-related reactions. Major risks are diarrhea (which can be severe), infusion-related reactions, left ventricular dysfunction with decreased ejection fraction, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer, as detected by an FDA-approved test
Treatment of adults with previously treated unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma

dosage.c: HER2-positive biliary tract cancer or gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma
dosage.d: 20 mg/kg by IV infusion once every 2 weeks
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; confirm HER2-positive status with an FDA-approved test

dosage.d: Withhold for grade 3 diarrhea despite optimal management, grade 2-3 infusion reactions, or asymptomatic LVEF decline; permanently discontinue for grade 4 diarrhea, grade 4 infusion reaction, or symptomatic heart failure
dosage.n: No dose reduction schedule defined; resume only when toxicity resolves to grade 1 or baseline

dosage.d: Premedicate 30-60 minutes before each infusion (e.g., acetaminophen, antihistamine, with or without corticosteroid per protocol)
dosage.n: Slowing or interrupting the infusion may be needed for infusion-related reactions

admin: Give 20 mg/kg as an intravenous infusion once every 2 weeks; do not give as IV push or bolus
Premedicate all patients 30 to 60 minutes before each dose to reduce infusion-related reactions
Use a sterile, preservative-free preparation; inspect for particulate matter and use the recommended infusion line filter per labeling
Monitor during the infusion and after completion for infusion-related reactions; slow, interrupt, or stop the infusion for reactions
Confirm HER2-positive status with an FDA-approved test before starting; assess LVEF at baseline and periodically
moa: Zanidatamab is a bispecific IgG1-like antibody that simultaneously binds two non-overlapping epitopes on HER2: extracellular domain 2 (ECD2, the pertuzumab site) and extracellular domain 4 (ECD4, the trastuzumab site). Biparatopic binding drives HER2 clustering, blocks ligand-independent signaling through MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways, promotes receptor internalization and downregulation, and engages Fc-mediated effector functions such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. This dual targeting produces activity in HER2-amplified tumors including biliary tract and gastric/GEJ adenocarcinomas.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to zanidatamab or any excipient
relative: Symptomatic heart failure or clinically significant decreased LVEF
History of severe infusion-related reaction to zanidatamab
Chronic diarrhea or colitis that would complicate GI toxicity
monitor: Infusion-related reaction symptoms during and after infusion
Left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and periodically
Pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential

preg: Based on its mechanism of HER2 blockade, zanidatamab can cause fetal harm including oligohydramnios and fetal abnormalities. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 4 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of zanidatamab in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 4 months after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is defined for renal impairment in the labeling summary. Monitor hydration and electrolytes closely if diarrhea occurs, and monitor overall tolerability.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment in the labeling summary. Monitor closely, particularly in biliary tract cancer with biliary obstruction, and adjust only for toxicity per labeling.

major: Other cardiotoxic or LVEF-lowering agents (e.g., anthracyclines) - additive left ventricular dysfunction; assess LVEF before combining
Other agents causing severe diarrhea - additive GI toxicity and dehydration risk
moderate: Antihypertensives in volume-depleted patients with diarrhea - risk of hypotension and renal injury; correct volume first
minor: Premedication agents (antihistamines, acetaminophen) - expected additive sedation with antihistamines only
interactions.food: Not applicable (IV); maintain oral hydration and electrolytes during diarrhea episodes.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol which may worsen diarrhea and dehydration.
interactions.diagnostics: Confirm HER2 positivity (IHC 3+) with an FDA-approved test; monitor LVEF by echocardiography or MUGA and monitor stool frequency and electrolytes.

serious: Severe diarrhea with dehydration and electrolyte loss
Left ventricular dysfunction with decreased ejection fraction and heart failure
emergency: Severe or bloody diarrhea with dizziness or reduced urination - seek urgent care
Chest pain, sudden breathlessness, or leg swelling (heart failure)
Breathing difficulty, throat tightness, or facial swelling during or after infusion

monitoring: Stool frequency, hydration, and electrolytes for diarrhea; start antidiarrheals promptly
Infusion-related reaction signs during and after each infusion
Left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and periodically, and for cardiac symptoms
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
Tumor response and HER2 test documentation
counsel: You will receive this drug as an IV infusion every 2 weeks, with medicines beforehand to lower infusion reaction risk
Diarrhea is very common and can be severe - tell your team at the first loose stool so treatment can start and fluids can be replaced
Report chills, fever, flushing, or trouble breathing during or after the infusion
Report new breathlessness, swelling of the legs, or fast weight gain (possible heart effects)
Use effective birth control during and for 4 months after treatment and do not breastfeed in that period
pk: HER2 target engagement from first infusion; tumor responses assessed over weeks
Elimination half-life on the order of days, supporting every-2-week dosing
Dosed every 2 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
Refrigerate lyophilized vials at 2-8 C; reconstituted and diluted solutions per labeling time limits; do not freeze or shake
pearls: First dual HER2-targeted bispecific antibody: binds ECD2 plus ECD4 on the same HER2 molecule for clustering and internalization
BTC indication requires HER2 IHC 3+ by an FDA-approved test; confirm before starting
Diarrhea is the dominant toxicity - start loperamide or per-protocol antidiarrheals early and monitor electrolytes
Premedicate every infusion and keep the infusion slow enough to manage reactions
Check LVEF at baseline and periodically; hold for asymptomatic decline and stop for symptomatic heart failure
missed: Zanidatamab is given as a supervised IV infusion every 2 weeks, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. If an appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule as soon as possible and maintain the every-2-week interval from the new date.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for zanidatamab overdose. Overdose may produce exaggerated diarrhea, infusion reactions, or cardiac effects. Stop or slow the infusion, monitor cardiac function, hydration, and electrolytes, and provide supportive care. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
